items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz Three tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting sea mines while attempting to cross an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in a statement shared on Thursday by state media. The tankers had switched off their radar and navigation systems and ignored warnings from the Guards' navy, which said the vessels had been abandoned on the southern shores of the strait. Reporting by Reuters

items.title: What the Midterms Mean for U.S. Foreign Policy
items.summary: If the polls are right, Democrats will retake at least one chamber of Congress in the U.S. midterms. And with voters focused on the cost of living, foreign policy is an unusually impactful driver at the ballot box: Tariffs have raised the price of everyday goods, and the war with Iran has sent gas prices soaring. How might Democrats use their new power over spending and oversight to challenge Trump’s agenda in his final two years in office? How will allies and adversaries read the results? Susan Glasser, a staff writer at the New Yorker and former editor in chief of Foreign Policy, will join FP Live to break down what the midterms mean for congressional power and for America’s standing in the world.

items.summary: Trump says 'could strike Iran tomorrow, or strike a beautiful deal' US President Donald Trump has said Washington could strike Iran "as soon as tomorrow", or reach a “big, beautiful” agreement with Tehran. “We’re thinking about doing it, and maybe tomorrow,” Trump told reporters when asked how far he is from a possible attack on Iran. “Do you really think I’m going to tell you if I’m going to do it?” he added. Trump said Iran "wanted to make a deal, but the problem is, will they hold the deal?” He repeated that his goal was to prevent Iran from eventually developing a nuclear weapon. “I’ve got to make it permanent,” he said. “That’s the only reason I’m doing it.” On Friday, Trump said at a rally that the US “may do another little epic fury”, using the codename of the US-Israeli war on Iran earlier this year.

items.title: Egypt calls for Yemen talks as parliament weighs military support to Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Egypt calls for Yemen talks as parliament weighs military support to Saudi Arabia Egypt advocates exploring "every opportunity" to resolve the Yemen war diplomatically, its foreign minister said, ahead of a parliamentary vote next week on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Iran-aligned Houthis. Any direct involvement of the Egyptian military, one of the region's largest, would raise the stakes in the fighting between the kingdom and the Houthis, an increasingly destabilising front in the spreading US-Israeli war on Iran. President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi called on Saturday for an urgent parliamentary session to authorise military involvement supporting the kingdom. After a closed session on Sunday, lawmakers postponed the vote until 26 October to allow more deliberation. Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday to deliver a letter from Sisi to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

items.summary: IRGC says three tankers hit mines crossing Hormuz Strait Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Tuesday that its naval mines halted three tankers attempting to travel the Strait of Hormuz via routes considered illegal by Tehran. "Two violating oil tankers were set ablaze and halted due to the explosion of mines planted by the brave sailors of the IRGC Navy at an illegal crossing point in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz," the IRGC said in a statement on its official Sepah News website. The Guard later said in a statement carried by state TV that a third oil tanker "exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine south of the Strait of Hormuz". The statement added that the tanker, "carrying over 2 million barrels of crude oil, had deactivated all of its radar and navigation systems".

The Iranian-backed Yemeni group has ramped up its attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, hitting oil facilities and airports among other targets, as Yemen's dormant civil war has roared back into life. Judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei and the supreme leader discussed issues including "securing public rights, and effectively combating corruption and its bottlenecks", the judiciary's Mizan Online website reported. items.summary: Trump says US could end Iran war quickly or let it 'wither' US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Washington could end the war with Iran quickly, but questioned whether to seek a swift conclusion or let the conflict wind down gradually. "We could end it very quickly," Trump said. "Do we want to finish it off or just want to let it wither?" Speaking to reporters on the White House South Lawn before departing for Florida, Trump said oil was passing through the Strait of Hormuz. "We are getting everything we want,” he said. He praised the US Navy for doing a “great job” of helping secure the passage of oil through the waterway and repeated his earlier claim that Hormuz was “totally ours and that’s the way we’ll keep it”.

items.summary: UN demands aid access to besieged Yemen city Taiz The United Nations insisted on Tuesday that aid must immediately be allowed to enter Yemen's Taiz, besieged by Iran-aligned Houthi fighters who are preventing supplies from reaching the country's third-largest city. Houthi fighters have encircled Taiz since early October, blocking the road that links it to Aden, interim capital of the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government. "Humanitarian aid must be immediately allowed to enter the city and its passage must be facilitated," UN human rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement. He said relief must reach the city to avert a rights catastrophe. "The Houthis' closure of the only supply route linking Taiz to Aden is placing civilians at grave risk, blocking humanitarian aid and cutting off essential supplies," said Turk.

The Sinjar Resistance Units (YBS), a group linked to the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), were formed in the 2000s to protect the Yazidi religious minority, who have faced discrimination and sectarian attacks for decades. They mobilised after August 2014 to fight the Islamic State group (IS), who carried out a genocide against the Yazidis in Sinjar, killing at least 5,000 people and abducting thousands of women and girls. And energy was the focus of Healey’s sole surprise in his consumer-facing policies – the £100 payment to 20m households in A-D council tax bands to help with fuel bills this winter. It will be funded, in effect, by tapping the banks for a few quid for 15 months via the bank surcharge. Continue reading...

clusters.headline: The Legacy of Reykjavik and the Future of U.S.–Russia Nuclear Relations

items.title: The Legacy of Reykjavik and the Future of U.S.–Russia Nuclear Relations
items.summary: On 11-12 October 1986, U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev met in Reykjavik, Iceland, hoping to achieve a groundbreaking agreement on controlling the world’s most dangerous weapons. While the summit yielded no agreement, it set in motion arms control negotiations tracks, held up the promise of nuclear disarmament, and contributed to the transformation of relations between two Cold War ach-adversaries. Forty years on, what lessons does Reykjavik hold for arms control, disarmament, and great power relations? To discuss the legacy of Reykjavik, Project on Managing the Atom (MTA) is honored to welcome Pavel Palazhchenko, former interpreter of Mikhail Gorbachev and an ambassador of the Gorbachev Foundation, David Holloway, Professor Emeritus of Stanford University and author of the International History of Nuclear Weapons, Matthew Bunn, Professor at Harvard Kennedy School, and Carol Saivetz, Senior Fellow at MIT Security Studies Program, with Mariana Budjeryn, MTA associate and a senior researcher at MIT as moderator.

items.summary: Why Hamas must not repeat Fatah's historic mistakes Submitted by Sami Al-Arian on Wed, 10/21/2026 - 16:18 The Cairo demands would bind Hamas to Fatah's recognition of Israel and the failed politics of Oslo, even as Israel's genocide in Gaza fuels wider scrutiny of Zionism A pedestrian walks past the closed Palestinian Legislative Council building in Ramallah on 11 October 2026, the day after Mahmoud Abbas postponed legislative elections to September 2027 (Zain Jaafar/AFP) Off As Israelis go to the polls in a general election , Palestinians have no vote of their own in sight. items.summary: Iran's supreme leader: A strong Iran rests upon scientific power In a statement shared by Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Monday, Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei emphasised the importance of scientific progress to Iran's strength. "The key to making Iran even stronger is the boundary-breaking work and problem-solving of the country's elites in scientific matters," Khamenei said in the statement addressed to Iranian elites and scientific and sporting medalists competing internationally. "The malice and crimes committed by the enemies of Islamic Iran against its scientists and elites demonstrate the effective role of elites in strengthening the country," Khamenei added, calling on officials to "provide necessary infrastructure" for a deep and rapid scientific leap. The statement was read at a ceremony honouring Iranian scientific and sports medalists, Tasnim reported.

Dit is besloten omdat de situatie in het Midden-Oosten op dit moment onvoorspelbaar is, zegt een woordvoerder. Om dezelfde reden zijn de vluchten op de luchthavens van Dammam en Riyad in Saudi-Arabië opgeschort tot 27 november. Na de Amerikaanse en Israëlische aanvallen op Iran in het voorjaar is het in de landen rond de Perzische Golf nooit rustig geweest. Iran blokkeert de doorvaart door de zeestraat en bestookt landen in de regio met raketten en drones. Houthi's uit Jemen vielen deze maand vliegvelden in Saudi-Arabië aan. Vorige week groeide de vrees voor nieuwe grootschalige Amerikaanse en Israëlische aanvallen op Iran en voor de reactie van Iran daarop. In verband met de oorlogshandelingen in het gebied vliegt KLM al bijna het hele jaar niet op Dammam, Riyad en Dubai. Het besluit om het niet vliegen op Dubai te verlengen tot het voorjaar (27 maart) vloeit voort uit een combinatie van factoren, zegt de woordvoerder. items.summary: Arriving in the White House in 2021, President Joe Biden set about dismantling much of his predecessor’s foreign-policy agenda. But there was one clear area of continuity: China. Here, Biden retained the first Trump administration’s confrontational approach, expanding the use of export controls on advanced technology and keeping China as the U.S. military’s pacing threat . items.title: Viva el Rey, de todos modos
items.summary: La visita triunfal de Felipe VI a Ceuta y Melilla es muy reveladora de la naturaleza de la monarquía en comparación con los demás regímenes políticos. Es imposible imaginar a ningún jefe de Gobierno español –ni de ningún otro país– aclamado durante una visita semejante. La explicación es sencilla: el Rey encarna a España , es España más allá de todas las divisiones partidistas. Solo un monarca, si su reinado es digno, puede encarnar así a toda una nación en un clima de unanimidad. Pero una monarquía no se improvisa; solo es legítima en la medida en que se inscribe en una larga historia. España tiene ese privilegio, al igual que los países escandinavos y Gran Bretaña. Pero la idea de la monarquía está lejos de ser estrictamente local, ni está anclada en el pasado, ni es arcaica. Addressing parliament, Qalibaf said the Iranian government would not be intimidated by US military threats or pressure and would defend what it considers the country’s territorial integrity. “Americans think that with a few levers of media pressure or military threats, they can make this great nation surrender to them,” he said, according to a report by Iran’s Tasnim news agency. “Unaware that today's Iran is not the Iran of the Pahlavi era of humiliation, but rather an impregnable fortress of self-confidence, defensive strength and iron will,” he added. Qalibaf said Iran was prepared to respond forcefully to any violation of its territory and insisted that threats of a wider war would not compel the country to abandon its interests. Ze filosofeerde over een betere wereld, maar was tegelijkertijd een getrouwde vrouw met kinderen die het huishouden moest doen. De hoofdpersoon wilde studeren en de wereld verbeteren, maar moest vechten voor haar kansen. Uiteindelijk kwam ze bij een internationale groep idealisten, feministen en anarchisten en hervond ze zichzelf. Wat de jury vooral boeiend vindt aan het boek is de "volstrekt originele manier" waarop Karssenberg de biografie heeft vormgegeven, zegt Spits. Op het spel staat een meerderheid in de twee Kamers van het Congres: het Huis van Afgevaardigden en de Senaat. De Republikeinen zetten alles op alles om hun meerderheden te behouden en de Democraten gaan op hun beurt tot het uiterste om die te veroveren. En ze zien een kans: in meerdere staten lijkt volgens de peilingen een verrassing mogelijk. Deze verkiezingen zijn voor Democraten dé mogelijkheid om de macht in Washington weer een beetje naar zich toe te trekken. De afgelopen twee jaar hebben Donald Trump en zijn Republikeinse partij met hun meerderheden in het Congres een stempel op het land en de wereld gedrukt. De acties van de president zijn voor veel mensen een reden om te gaan stemmen bij de midterm elections . Vaak worden tussentijdse verkiezingen gezien als indirect referendum over de president. clusters.headline: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield

items.title: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield
items.summary: We’ve heard much about the end of the west. At the proposed summit between Trump, Putin and Xi, those fears could crystallise In the final two years of a US presidency, when Congress has been lost, approval ratings have sunk like a stone and their party has started to think about who’s coming next, the person occupying the Oval Office can feel their power draining away. Domestic legislation, particularly in an era where bipartisan cooperation is almost nonexistent, grinds to a halt. But as the days tick by until the end, and as presidents begin to think about their legacy, there is one part of the job where they still have power: the rest of the world. In the final weeks of his presidency in 1992 George HW Bush sent 28,000 American troops to Somalia to help end a famine. For Bill Clinton, it was a quixotic attempt to bring peace to the Middle East by ending the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Barack Obama restored diplomatic ties with Cuba, making a historic visit to Havana, as well as a final, successful push on the Iran nuclear deal. Continue reading...

clusters.headline: What Israel's razor thin elections mean for Gaza and Iran

items.title: What Israel's razor thin elections mean for Gaza and Iran
items.summary: Israelis head to the polls on October 27 in a vote that will cast Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing and religious allies against a motley crew of opposition parties. At the moment, neither side is expected to have a clear path to the 61-seat majority needed to form a government in the 120-seat Knesset. Netanyahu and his leading opponent are only projected to win some 20 seats each, but the biggest party doesn’t necessarily get the right to form the government. clusters.headline: Ahead of US and Israeli elections, 3-day joint attack on Iran 'would not radically change conflict'

items.title: Ahead of US and Israeli elections, 3-day joint attack on Iran 'would not radically change conflict'
items.summary: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome Federico Donelli, Associate Professor of International Relations in the Department of Political and Social Sciences at the University of Trieste in Italy. Can another three days of military strikes achieve what eight months of confrontation have failed to deliver? Donelli challenges the assumption that a short, intensive offensive would necessarily produce a decisive political outcome. He argues, "the real question is whether military pressure is intended to constrain Iran's capacity, or to pressure Iran to sit on the table." And whether they can translate that capacity into a sustainable political outcome without provoking a wider regional crisis. Regardless, Donelli reminds us that "Iran still has leverage over the US."

items.summary: Het Europees Parlement heeft het Internationaal Strafhof (ICC) in Den Haag gekozen als de winnaar van de Sacharovprijs van dit jaar. Het hof staat onder zware druk van de Verenigde Staten . President Trump wil met sancties het hof platleggen. "Met de toekenning van de prijs aan het Strafhof erkent het Europarlement het belangrijke werk van het hof bij het handhaven van het internationaal recht en de internationale rechtspraak", zegt parlementsvoorzitter Roberta Metsola. Wat doet het Internationaal Strafhof? Het Strafhof onderzoekt, vervolgt en berecht personen die worden beschuldigd van mensenrechtenschendingen en dient als aanvulling op de nationale rechtbanken van aangesloten landen. Het hof doet onder meer onderzoek naar genocide, oorlogsmisdaden en misdaden tegen de menselijkheid. Alle landen in de Europese Unie zijn verplicht om besluiten van het Strafhof uit te voeren, vanwege het Statuut van Rome. Het hof wordt niet door alle landen in de wereld erkend. Amerikaanse functionarissen beweren dat een laatste grootschalige, driedaagse aanval genoeg economische schade kan aanrichten om Iran tot concessies te dwingen. Het is onduidelijk hoe een aanval - bijna acht maanden na de eerste Israëlisch-Amerikaanse aanvallen - de Iraanse regering nu wel op de knieën kan krijgen. items.title: Was the MOU meant to be trashed?
items.summary: As President Trump appeared to accept an end to the Iran war by agreeing to the short-lived Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on June 17, many Republican senators were deeply alarmed. Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.) openly trashed the agreement, warning Ronald Reagan was “ rolling over in his grave ,” before getting into a war of words with President Donald Trump over the administration’s strategy. Yet opposition to the MOU with Iran abruptly softened. Cassidy received a briefing from Vice President JD Vance and Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff that convinced him to flip his votes on future war powers resolutions on Iran. He suggested afterwards that the administration had a “ plausible plan ” to accomplish many of the war’s original goals to destroy or degrade Iran’s nuclear program, ballistic missiles and conventional warfare capabilities. items.title: American farmers are slammed by war 7,000 miles away
items.summary: American farmers are in crisis, facing rising costs, disrupted export markets, and mounting financial pressure. While farming has always faced unavoidable challenges, such as weather, pests, and the vagaries of demand, the present problems are entirely of Washington’s making. The Trump administration’s tariffs have damaged critical trading relations, and its war against Iran has disrupted energy and fertilizer trade through the Strait of Hormuz. Washington’s response to beleaguered American agricultural interests has been billions of dollars in emergency aid and promises that future trade deals will deliver additional relief. It is a familiar cycle: Washington creates new risks for American producers, taxpayers absorb part of the resulting losses, and the underlying policies remain in place. Farmers receive temporary assistance but are left to navigate the same uncertain markets and elevated costs that made the assistance necessary. I passanti si fermano, ridono, insultano il finto presidente americano e riprendono la scena con i cellulari. Tutto ciò arriva mentre i rapporti tra Washington e Teheran sono nuovamente in stallo. items.title: The Guardian view on the Republicans’ midterms struggle: Trump has circuses, but voters also want bread | Editorial
items.summary: As prices keep rising, more of the president’s supporters are asking what happened to the economic good times he promised It is no great revelation that Donald Trump is enriching himself as president. He raked in $2.2bn in 2025, with his position and his personal interests frequently overlapping. Yet this week’s poll finding that 34% of Republicans (and 66% of all American voters) think that he is using his position to make himself rich merits attention . Separately, voters in a Fox News poll last week put government corruption at the top of their list of concerns – just ahead of inflation and high prices. Mr Trump pledged that people would be better off if they voted for him. Billionaires are; not the rest. He promised to lower grocery costs (they have risen) and to cut the price of gasoline to below $2 a gallon. It’s more than double that, thanks to his illegal war on Iran. Tariffs haven’t helped. Just a few days after his diesel deal with the Kremlin, the US president said Zelenskyy was more difficult to deal with than Vladimir Putin and blamed Ukraine’s leader for rocketing oil prices – without any reference to the impact of his own war on Iran. Nearly 20% identified as “pure independents,” while 35% said they were Democrats. Though Republicans surveyed in the poll backed Operation Epic Fury at a rate of 77% to 16%, overwhelming opposition among Democrats and independents left respondents opposed to the war overall, 49% to 44%. items.title: How the UAE and MEK weaponize AI to spread propaganda
items.summary: Somewhere inside Iran, a network of activists exchanged messages about politics and news with an activist — nicknamed “Parsa” — on the messaging app Telegram. They had no idea they were actually speaking to an AI agent that had copied the real activist’s style by training it on 8,400 real Telegram posts. Instead of “Parsa,” they were actually communicating with the People’s Mojahedin Organization of Iran (MEK), an Iranian Islamist-Marxist opposition group widely regarded as a cult. According to a report from Anthropic released last month, this operation was carried out by four individuals working for the MEK. They built an AI agent named “Viktor” that also surveilled individuals inside Iran and flooded social media platforms with pro-MEK content under “independent” branding. The Anthropic report sheds light on how foreign actors are increasingly using artificial intelligence tools like Claude and ChatGPT for their influence operations. items.title: As Houthis encircle Taiz, Yemen's Saudi-backed gov't faces disaster
items.summary: Taiz, Yemen’s third-largest city, endured a siege from 2015 to 2017. Today, it is encircled again. The World Food Program says it cannot reach more than 600,000 people in and around the city. The International Organization for Migration counts over 200,000 people displaced since the Houthi offensive on Yemen’s Red Sea coast launched in September. Why this city, and why now? The Houthis, formally known as the Ansar Allah movement, draw their strength from the Zaydi Shia highlands of the north. Critics say their governing ideology rests on the belief that the right to rule belongs to sayyids , descendants of the Prophet Mohammad, a lineage to which the Houthi family itself belongs. The Houthis have long denied seeking to restore the Imamate, but in Taiz, which has for a decade resisted Houthi encroachment, that denial finds few believers. Taiz has a long history of political activism and hostility to the idea of religious hereditary rule. items.title: Vast, variabel of dynamisch? Huishoudens op zoek naar juiste energiecontract

Terwijl de bedrijven hoge winsten behalen, blijven de energietarieven voor consumenten alsmaar oplopen. En dat levert de vraag op: kun je het beste een vast, variabel of toch dynamisch contract afsluiten? Verschillende energiebedrijven maakten de torenhoge winsten bekend die ze de afgelopen drie maanden hebben gemaakt. Zo zagen Shell en Vattenfall hun winst verdubbelen door de hoge olie- en gasprijs. Ondertussen kwam de gasprijs voor een megawattuur gisteren voor het eerst sinds het najaar van 2022 boven de 100 euro uit. De stijgende gasrekening leidt tot vragen bij de Consumentenbond. "Heel veel vragen van mensen over wat ze moeten doen. Het leeft ontzettend", zegt Joyce Donat van de Consumentenbond. Ook consumentencollectief United Consumers ziet dat klanten op zoek zijn naar antwoorden en zekerheid. Toch is er geen pasklaar antwoord. It took weeks of debate in the halls of power for the parliament to ultimately give Sisi the greenlight. This is unusual given that the chamber is largely pro-government and normally gives the president what he asks for. A handful of members abstained over concerns that relevant details — such as the length of the mission, the cost, how many troops would be sent — were never disclosed. Their complaints reflect deep unease in Egypt about being dragged into a foreign war. items.title: Could the path to US-Iran diplomacy run through Moscow?
items.summary: During a meeting last week with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff, Russian President Vladimir Putin offered to help broker a deal to end the U.S.-Iran war. The proposal — the latest in a series of recent Russian offers to act as an intermediary between Washington and Tehran — has a certain logic to it. While the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has brought Russia some economic gains through rising energy prices, Moscow fears further escalation and spillover across the Persian Gulf and parts of the former Soviet space. Russia is also one of Iran’s closest partners and one of the world’s leading exporters of enriched uranium, meaning that it could help break the impasse over domestic Iranian nuclear enrichment. Yet Moscow will struggle to gain Western and Gulf Arab acceptance as a mediator, particularly amid the Ukraine conflict and heightened threat perceptions of Iran in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) while Russia is increasingly aligned with Iran. items.title: What the Midterms Mean for U.S. Foreign Policy
items.summary: If the polls are right, Democrats will retake at least one chamber of Congress in the U.S. midterms. And with voters focused on the cost of living, foreign policy is an unusually impactful driver at the ballot box: Tariffs have raised the price of everyday goods, and the war with Iran has sent gas prices soaring. How might Democrats use their new power over spending and oversight to challenge Trump’s agenda in his final two years in office? How will allies and adversaries read the results? Susan Glasser, a staff writer at the New Yorker and former editor in chief of Foreign Policy, will join FP Live to break down what the midterms mean for congressional power and for America’s standing in the world.

items.title: The Legacy of Reykjavik and the Future of U.S.–Russia Nuclear Relations
items.summary: On 11-12 October 1986, U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev met in Reykjavik, Iceland, hoping to achieve a groundbreaking agreement on controlling the world’s most dangerous weapons. While the summit yielded no agreement, it set in motion arms control negotiations tracks, held up the promise of nuclear disarmament, and contributed to the transformation of relations between two Cold War ach-adversaries. Forty years on, what lessons does Reykjavik hold for arms control, disarmament, and great power relations? To discuss the legacy of Reykjavik, Project on Managing the Atom (MTA) is honored to welcome Pavel Palazhchenko, former interpreter of Mikhail Gorbachev and an ambassador of the Gorbachev Foundation, David Holloway, Professor Emeritus of Stanford University and author of the International History of Nuclear Weapons, Matthew Bunn, Professor at Harvard Kennedy School, and Carol Saivetz, Senior Fellow at MIT Security Studies Program, with Mariana Budjeryn, MTA associate and a senior researcher at MIT as moderator.

Each time, after protesting, the U.S. chose to give in. And each time, the promised silver bullet failed to solve Kyiv’s battlefield challenges. items.summary: Iran's supreme leader: A strong Iran rests upon scientific power In a statement shared by Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Monday, Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei emphasised the importance of scientific progress to Iran's strength. "The key to making Iran even stronger is the boundary-breaking work and problem-solving of the country's elites in scientific matters," Khamenei said in the statement addressed to Iranian elites and scientific and sporting medalists competing internationally. items.summary: La visita triunfal de Felipe VI a Ceuta y Melilla es muy reveladora de la naturaleza de la monarquía en comparación con los demás regímenes políticos. Es imposible imaginar a ningún jefe de Gobierno español –ni de ningún otro país– aclamado durante una visita semejante. La explicación es sencilla: el Rey encarna a España , es España más allá de todas las divisiones partidistas. Solo un monarca, si su reinado es digno, puede encarnar así a toda una nación en un clima de unanimidad. Pero una monarquía no se improvisa; solo es legítima en la medida en que se inscribe en una larga historia. España tiene ese privilegio, al igual que los países escandinavos y Gran Bretaña. Pero la idea de la monarquía está lejos de ser estrictamente local, ni está anclada en el pasado, ni es arcaica. items.summary: Schrijver Maite Karssenberg krijgt de Libris Geschiedenis Prijs voor haar biografie Dubbelleven. Geertruida Kapteyn-Muysken en haar rebelse levensfilosofie. De prijs voor het beste geschiedenisboek van het jaar werd uitgereikt door juryvoorzitter Frits Spits in een speciale uitzending van het VPRO-radioprogramma OVT. Karssenberg krijgt 20.000 euro. 'Schrikbarend ondergeschikt' Het boek legt de "schrikbarend ondergeschikte rol van de vrouw in de 19e eeuw bloot", zegt de jury. Geertruida Kapteyn-Muysken leefde van 1855 tot 1920. Ze filosofeerde over een betere wereld, maar was tegelijkertijd een getrouwde vrouw met kinderen die het huishouden moest doen. De hoofdpersoon wilde studeren en de wereld verbeteren, maar moest vechten voor haar kansen. Uiteindelijk kwam ze bij een internationale groep idealisten, feministen en anarchisten en hervond ze zichzelf. Wat de jury vooral boeiend vindt aan het boek is de "volstrekt originele manier" waarop Karssenberg de biografie heeft vormgegeven, zegt Spits. items.title: IRGC spokesman says war could have consequences beyond Iran's borders
items.summary: IRGC spokesman says war could have consequences beyond Iran's borders Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Spokesman Hossein Mohebbi has warned that the US-Israeli war against Iran could have consequences beyond the country’s borders, Press TV reported on Saturday. Mohebbi described the confrontation as an “apocalyptic war” and said Iran would achieve “absolute victory” and emerge as a global superpower. He urged Iranians to maintain national unity and rely on domestic capabilities, arguing that the conflict extended beyond the battlefield to encompass the country’s cultural, religious and civilisational identity. The IRGC spokesman accused the United States and Israel of seeking to weaken and fragment Iran by undermining its identity and replacing its culture with their own values.

items.title: Iran judiciary says chief holds rare meeting with supreme leader

Mojtaba was chosen in March to succeed his father and longtime ruler Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in US-Israeli strikes in central Tehran alongside senior military commanders at the start of the Middle East war, and was said to have been injured in the same attack. Judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei and the supreme leader discussed issues including "securing public rights, and effectively combating corruption and its bottlenecks", the judiciary's Mizan Online website reported. They held talks on "pursuing the recovery of rights and compensation for material and moral damages arising from the crimes of American-Zionist criminals", it said.

items.title: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield
items.summary: We’ve heard much about the end of the west. At the proposed summit between Trump, Putin and Xi, those fears could crystallise In the final two years of a US presidency, when Congress has been lost, approval ratings have sunk like a stone and their party has started to think about who’s coming next, the person occupying the Oval Office can feel their power draining away. Domestic legislation, particularly in an era where bipartisan cooperation is almost nonexistent, grinds to a halt. But as the days tick by until the end, and as presidents begin to think about their legacy, there is one part of the job where they still have power: the rest of the world. In the final weeks of his presidency in 1992 George HW Bush sent 28,000 American troops to Somalia to help end a famine. For Bill Clinton, it was a quixotic attempt to bring peace to the Middle East by ending the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Barack Obama restored diplomatic ties with Cuba, making a historic visit to Havana, as well as a final, successful push on the Iran nuclear deal. Continue reading...

Speaking on condition of anonymity, the officials gave few details and did not say how or where Tehran would carry out such attacks. The second official said Washington’s Gulf allies, which have invested heavily in such infrastructure, “should hold Washington, not Tehran, responsible for any damage to undersea cables.” Yadollah Javani, the deputy head of political affairs for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said on Wednesday that Iran could target seven major internet cables

items.title: Trump says US could end Iran war quickly or let it 'wither'
items.summary: Trump says US could end Iran war quickly or let it 'wither' US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Washington could end the war with Iran quickly, but questioned whether to seek a swift conclusion or let the conflict wind down gradually. "We could end it very quickly," Trump said. "Do we want to finish it off or just want to let it wither?" Speaking to reporters on the White House South Lawn before departing for Florida, Trump said oil was passing through the Strait of Hormuz. "We are getting everything we want,” he said. He praised the US Navy for doing a “great job” of helping secure the passage of oil through the waterway and repeated his earlier claim that Hormuz was “totally ours and that’s the way we’ll keep it”.

items.title: Egypt calls for Yemen talks as parliament weighs military support to Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Egypt calls for Yemen talks as parliament weighs military support to Saudi Arabia Egypt advocates exploring "every opportunity" to resolve the Yemen war diplomatically, its foreign minister said, ahead of a parliamentary vote next week on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Iran-aligned Houthis. Any direct involvement of the Egyptian military, one of the region's largest, would raise the stakes in the fighting between the kingdom and the Houthis, an increasingly destabilising front in the spreading US-Israeli war on Iran. President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi called on Saturday for an urgent parliamentary session to authorise military involvement supporting the kingdom. After a closed session on Sunday, lawmakers postponed the vote until 26 October to allow more deliberation. Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday to deliver a letter from Sisi to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

The Iranian-backed Yemeni group has ramped up its attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, hitting oil facilities and airports among other targets, as Yemen's dormant civil war has roared back into life. The world's largest oil exporter, Saudi Arabia, has had its crude shipments squeezed by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthis' declaration of a maritime blockade. But shipments continue to move despite the conflicts, Jihad Azour told AFP.

items.title: Ahead of US and Israeli elections, 3-day joint attack on Iran 'would not radically change conflict'
items.summary: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome Federico Donelli, Associate Professor of International Relations in the Department of Political and Social Sciences at the University of Trieste in Italy. Can another three days of military strikes achieve what eight months of confrontation have failed to deliver? Donelli challenges the assumption that a short, intensive offensive would necessarily produce a decisive political outcome. He argues, "the real question is whether military pressure is intended to constrain Iran's capacity, or to pressure Iran to sit on the table." And whether they can translate that capacity into a sustainable political outcome without provoking a wider regional crisis. Regardless, Donelli reminds us that "Iran still has leverage over the US."

Wat doet het Internationaal Strafhof? Het Strafhof onderzoekt, vervolgt en berecht personen die worden beschuldigd van mensenrechtenschendingen en dient als aanvulling op de nationale rechtbanken van aangesloten landen. Het hof doet onder meer onderzoek naar genocide, oorlogsmisdaden en misdaden tegen de menselijkheid. Alle landen in de Europese Unie zijn verplicht om besluiten van het Strafhof uit te voeren, vanwege het Statuut van Rome. Het hof wordt niet door alle landen in de wereld erkend. items.summary: Qatar, France issue joint statement calling for the implementation of Gaza ceasefire French President Emmanuel Macron held discussions with Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani during Macron’s visit to Doha, regarding the situation in Iran, Gaza and Lebanon and the need for diplomacy to ensure regional stability. They said the crossing was “closed to passengers, vehicles and commercial trucks until further notice”. A separate source told Reuters that authorities made the decision to review security arrangements at the crossing. An Iraqi government source earlier told Al Jazeera that the government had ordered the closure but gave no reason. items.summary: Death toll from Houthi strike on Yemen government camp rises to 73 Local Yemeni authorities on Tuesday raised the death toll from a Houthi strike a day earlier on a military camp belonging to government forces to 73, as fighting between the foes escalates. It marked the deadliest attack in weeks as fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognised, Saudi-supported government rages after the collapse of a years-long truce. The death toll from Monday's strike on the camp in the energy-rich Shabwa province "increased to 73 martyrs, while search and follow-up efforts are ongoing to discover the fate of 14 missing people", authorities said in a statement. Local authorities had put the death toll at 53 on Monday, adding that more than 200 others were injured, all new members of the internal security forces who were undergoing training.

items.summary: IRGC says three tankers hit mines crossing Hormuz Strait Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Tuesday that its naval mines halted three tankers attempting to travel the Strait of Hormuz via routes considered illegal by Tehran. "Two violating oil tankers were set ablaze and halted due to the explosion of mines planted by the brave sailors of the IRGC Navy at an illegal crossing point in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz," the IRGC said in a statement on its official Sepah News website. The Guard later said in a statement carried by state TV that a third oil tanker "exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine south of the Strait of Hormuz". The statement added that the tanker, "carrying over 2 million barrels of crude oil, had deactivated all of its radar and navigation systems".

items.title: Iran security chief rejects moving enriched uranium out of country
items.summary: Iran security chief rejects moving enriched uranium out of country Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei on Tuesday told the visiting Pakistani army chief Asim Munir that Tehran would not allow nuclear material to leave the country, according to state TV. "Not even a tiny bit of enriched nuclear material will leave Iran; such materials constitute a major asset and national wealth for the Iranian people, intended for use within the country," said Rezaei, Iran's secretary of the Supreme National Security Council. "There will be no negotiations until America takes steps to build trust - a process that must begin with the fulfilment of Iran's conditions," he added. Iran's chief negotiator and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf made similar remarks to Munir, who is in Tehran as part of a renewed push to mediate a peace deal between the Islamic Republic and the United States.

items.title: UN demands aid access to besieged Yemen city Taiz
items.summary: UN demands aid access to besieged Yemen city Taiz The United Nations insisted on Tuesday that aid must immediately be allowed to enter Yemen's Taiz, besieged by Iran-aligned Houthi fighters who are preventing supplies from reaching the country's third-largest city. Houthi fighters have encircled Taiz since early October, blocking the road that links it to Aden, interim capital of the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government. "Humanitarian aid must be immediately allowed to enter the city and its passage must be facilitated," UN human rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement. He said relief must reach the city to avert a rights catastrophe. "The Houthis' closure of the only supply route linking Taiz to Aden is placing civilians at grave risk, blocking humanitarian aid and cutting off essential supplies," said Turk.

The International Organization for Migration counts over 200,000 people displaced since the Houthi offensive on Yemen’s Red Sea coast launched in September. Why this city, and why now? The Houthis, formally known as the Ansar Allah movement, draw their strength from the Zaydi Shia highlands of the north. Critics say their governing ideology rests on the belief that the right to rule belongs to sayyids , descendants of the Prophet Mohammad, a lineage to which the Houthi family itself belongs. The Houthis have long denied seeking to restore the Imamate, but in Taiz, which has for a decade resisted Houthi encroachment, that denial finds few believers. Taiz has a long history of political activism and hostility to the idea of religious hereditary rule.
